Vanrahar (R77)

Scoring-table region: Rahen.

In one sentence: Build a jungle paradise from the Harimari states of the Ascension Peninsula, restore the old Harimraj, and pay for it with rigid caste hierarchy and human forced labour.

v2.1 personality coordinates: Expansion 93/100 | Authoritarianism 90/100 | Magic ↔ Artifice 50/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 15/100) | Pluralism 8/100.

v2.1 values: Evil (26/100), trajectory deteriorating.

Story: high | Mission-tree length: medium-long (33 direct R77 mission definitions) | Mission-tree version: local v1.37.5.0 scripts; a 2026 development diary mentions a rework | Distinctiveness: high | Prison difficulty: medium-high | Early pressure: medium-high | Expansion: high.

An Ancient Name, a Future Flag

Vanrahar is not a ready-made kingdom on the 1444 map. The native R77 history file lists a preset government, Royal Harimari culture, High Philosophy, and a capital, but no reigning 1444 monarch. The player must start from an eligible Primordial Harimari country, meet core-province, Ascension Peninsula control, religion, army-tradition, and peace conditions, then use the decision to become R77 and receive its distinctive mission tree. Tujgal, Umdaj, and Rabaghekhur have missions connected to this formation line; they are narrative entrances, not the only predecessors, and their opening rulers must not be written as Vanrahar rulers.【Local script】【Local localisation】

The state borrows the memory of an ancient Harimari empire. The offline English Harimar and Harimraj entries record Harimar’s unification of the Harimari, the establishment of the Harimraj around 48, and its later reach across Rahen and beyond, followed by fragmentation, outside conquest, and revival. The local Vanrahar page is sparse. The old kingdom’s glory belongs to the pre-start setting and does not mean R77 has already unified the region in 1444.【Wiki material】

The 2020 Rahen development diary presents Vanrahar as a militarized, conservative formable seeking to recover an old order. The current tree follows that direction, but the old diary establishes design context, not every current reward; a 2026 official diary mentioning a rework cannot establish the version of every locally installed reward merely through its publication date.【Official development diary】

Beyond Restoration: Who Rules Whom

The current structured data counts 33 direct R77 mission definitions, while Vanrahar_Missions.txt retains conditional post-formation groups for different predecessors. The main line moves from coastal defence into inner Rahen and regional hegemony, then toward Harimari Rule and Overlord of Dhujat; later content includes training facilities, warrior housing, and the Vanrahar Academy. It combines homeland development with an expansionist project to reshape Raheni order through force.【Local script】【Local localisation】

The clearest and darkest turn is enslaving humans. The missions require rigid caste mobility, low human tolerance, and a specified number of owned, stable provinces with human minorities. After completion, owned human-culture provinces receive a permanent modifier that facilitates cultural conversion and yields political resources when conversion occurs. The flavour text classifies humans and other peoples as low castes serving the upper orders. The value issue is institutional lowering of other sapient groups and the use of their labour and status as instruments of rule, not Harimari identity, war, or cultural difference itself.【Local script】【Local flavour text】

The predecessor choices create narrative tension. The Tujgal line leans toward a purified jungle paradise; Umdaj faces whether to choose a more modern alternative state form; Rabaghekhur may begin by defending the old Raj order. The formation decision does not make R43, R45, and R50 the only legal entrances, so they remain examples with explicit mission links rather than a single fixed dynasty’s straight-line restoration.【Local script】

What It Feels Like to Play

Early play uses a Harimari predecessor to stabilize the Ascension Peninsula, build army tradition, and control the required formation region. After the Tag change, the R77 tree contests Rahen and positions farther afield. The late game turns caste, cultural conversion, and military education into durable state institutions alongside high-intensity war. Numerous conditions and broad geography make waiting and grind come from formation, military-political integration, and long fronts rather than one disaster countdown. Player posts praise the new military strength and mission narrative, but their versions, strategies and campaign results remain personal experiences.【Local script】【Community viewpoint】

The assessment is Expansion 93/100 | Authoritarianism 90/100 | Magic—Artifice 50/100 (intensity 15) | Pluralism 8/100 and Evil 26/100, deteriorating. Academies and military organization provide construction benefits, but human forced labour, low tolerance, and rigid caste are stronger negative evidence. The judgment is based on concrete institutions, not Harimari identity, monarchy, or expansion. It suits players seeking a militarized formable, the Harimari homeland, and a harsh institutional narrative; players seeking an egalitarian federation or low-intensity trade development should avoid it.【Local script】 Detailed formation conditions, sources and historical boundaries remain on the original research evidence page; this batch's English checks are recorded in the additional receipt.

National Ideas (Reference Appendix)

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and scripted effects. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as idea groups are filled, and the ambition applies after all seven have been unlocked. Racial, government and mission rewards are excluded, and successor sets do not automatically stack with predecessor ideas. Descriptions may recall history or portray future ideals, not automatically events already completed in 1444. Native English originals are reused rather than back-translating expanded Chinese localisation. Inherited effect-display values and any unresolved unit caveats are retained without changing Chinese source data.

Vanrahar (R77) — Vanrahari Ideas

Traditions: Vanrahari Traditions

Effects: Army morale: +20%; Land leader shock: +1.

Idea 1: Harimari Chargers

Few things are as scary as an angry tiger out for your blood. The harimari know that well enough, and while many still use that, the majority has grown decadent and philosophical. In Vanrahar they put the youngest most aggressive males in the front line, when it's their turn they will quickly charge their enemies with the unbound ferocity of youth. This devastating charge is then followed up by the steady march and charge of more experienced veterans, to double down on the devastating charge and to leave no time to recover.

Effects: Shock damage: +20%.

Idea 2: Tooth and Claw

While it has been many centuries since the harimari ascended from their primal roots, their savagery arises easily during combat. They are fierce warriors with weapons, but even a disarmed harimari is a threat. All harimari have relied on this ferocity, however in Vanrahar they doubled down on this strength. The warriors from the ancient homelands are seen as some of the strongest in all of Haless.

Effects: Infantry combat ability: +15%.

Idea 3: In the Footsteps of Harimar

It has been 1500 years since Harimar led the harimari from the jungles that now make up the heartland of Vanrahar and out to conquer all of Rahen and Haless. Many things can be said about his policies and other reforms, but at the core of his success lies his military genius. In response the harimari from Vanrahar doubled down on their military education in the hopes of creating a new Harimar.

Effects: Monarch military skill: +1.

Idea 4: Expanded Warrior Caste

While in most harimari nations the warrior caste has a role below the philosopher and administrative caste, in Vanrahar the importance of the warrior caste has been raised above their more intellectually inclined brothers.

Effects: Infantry Cost: -10%.

Idea 5: 'I Sad Jahar Bhagera'

'The Ten Thousand Panthers' is the name of an epic poem about a mythical unit of elite forces that fought many battles under the command of Harimar. They underwent many hardships and losses but always came out on top at the end. Finally the unit was wiped out in a heroic last stand as they stood their ground against an army twenty times their number. Supposedly they broke their enemies despite having been completely destroyed and Harimar considered it a tragic victory, but a victory nonetheless. The tales of their exploits inspire a great number young harimari from Vanrahar to pursue a military career.

Effects: global_manpower_modifier：+15%.

Idea 6: Cruel Masters

While other harimari adopted a tolerant policy towards their human subjects, in Vanrahar they considered the human castes lower in every sense of the word. They existed purely to feed the economy and war machine of the nation. The taskmasters of Vanrahar were then also not shy in cracking down on any unrest. And they were certainly not afraid to use force.

Effects: Harsh treatment cost: -20%.

Idea 7: Adapt to Firearms

With the adoption of firearm techniques and improved muskets by the rest of the world, the harimari of Vanrahar realised they had to adapt. Though loathe to properly adopt the muskets of other cultures, they instead developed techniques to reduce casualties to both cannon and musket fire. They approached the enemy lines in more spread out formations before converging on the enemy in a rapid charge.

Effects: fire_damage_received：-10%.

Ambition: Vanrahari Ambition

Effects: army_tradition_decay：-0.01.

Tujgal (R43) — Tujgal Ideas

Traditions: Tujgal Traditions

Effects: Infantry combat ability: +10%; Army maintenance modifier: -5%.

Idea 1: The White Tiger

'Tyger Tyger, burning bright, In the forests of the night; What immortal hand or eye, Could frame thy fearful symmetry?

In what distant deeps or skies Burnt the fire of thine eyes? On what wings dare he aspire? What the hand, dare seize the fire?

And what shoulder, & what art, Could twist the sinews of thy heart? And when thy heart began to beat, What dread hand? & what dread feet?'

Effects: Shock damage: +10%.

Idea 2: Adherents of the Old Ways

When our people were first endowed with higher intellect and clawed their way into sapience, the rule of the jungle was our law, and strength was the right by which we asserted dominance. With martial spirit did Harimar, Greatest of Us, win supremacy over the men of Haless, and while many of our cousins have fallen into lazy decadence in golden palaces throughout the east, we in Tujgal have not forgotten the rule of Tooth and Claw.

Here, the martial spirit of our folk is undiminished, and by right of might we will once more rule.

Effects: Army morale: +10%.

Idea 3: The Ending Games

A series of trials and war games intended to train the youth into the next generation of excellent generals and officers, the Ending Games were a series of exams that every harimari youth was exposed to in their 14th year. Testing not only physical skill and tactical acumen but emotional durability and willingness to self-sacrifice, the Ending Games were a grueling challenge that were criticized for the extreme mental trauma and physical damage it exposed the youth to.

Despite this struggle, there was no denying that the cohorts that passed through the Ending Games together were knit together into unbreakable bonds of camaraderie that would instill the whole of the population of Tujgal with both knowledge of war and the means of prosecuting those wars.

Effects: Army tradition: +0.5.

Idea 4: The Pahruavan Feud

The Mangrove forest of Pahruavan, where the shadows are long, the waters warm, and the hunting good - many poets have opined it the finest piece of land in all of the Ascension Peninsula. Though it was ruled by Tujgal for many years, the scheming lords of Rabaghekhur conspired with the decadent Rajas to seize the land in the 1380s under the guise of protecting the coast from invasion by Bhuvauri, and piratical incursions. Though we protested, our voices were ignored and our lands occupied 'to keep the peace'.

Since this betrayal, we have nursed our grudge, and the reclamation of Pahruavan has always been the foremost military goal of the prabhi of Tujgal. We were rewarded for our patience when, in 1502, the slave lords of Bhuvauri approached us with a plan to crush Rabaghekhur while the armies of the Raj's were embroiled in the 2nd War of the Vizierate. Together we launched a joint invasion, with our armies seizing Pahruavan while the Bhuvauri retook Sardika, burning Rabaghekhur’s fleet in the process port. The cowardly Senapti of Rabaghekhur, seeing our unstoppable advance, fled, and we stood alone atop the hierarchy of the Harimari homeland. Moving quickly, we elicited oaths of loyalty from the Oghaprabhi who controlled the thousand small holdings of the peninsula, marking the beginning of Tujgali hegemony in the south.

Effects: Core-creation cost: -15%.

Idea 5: Centralization of the Jungles

For over a thousand years, the governance of the Ascension Peninsula has been managed through the Oghaprabhi system, wherein individual harimari lords have controlled personal hunting territories in the Raj's stead. While effective at keeping the peninsula peaceful, the system proved woefully inadequate for centrally managing the realm.

It was replaced instead with a new model of control based on the governorships of Bulwari realms such as those ruled by the Jaddari, wherein local rulers were rotated to various realms often enough that they could not establish local powerbases in individual corners of the Peninsula. This system broke the back of the local landlords, and though many minor noble revolts made the initial implementation of the system rocky, the efficiency of such a system proved its worth in the long term.

Effects: global_autonomy：-0.05%.

Idea 6: The Idea of Vanrahar

When central Rahen descended into chaos following the invasion of the Jadd Empire, Tujgal stood strong in the jungles of the south, rebuffing any elven advance into the homeland and offering hope of salvation to those small powers that dwelled nearby. In exchange for our protection, the former Prabhi of Amtujsaat, Umdaj, and Parus Panasur became vassals of Tujgal in the so-called Union of Umdaj, an event which united the entirety of the Ascension Peninsula under one strong ruler for the first time in centuries.

In the aftermath of this unification, the idea of a single, unified harimari state grew popular among the population of the peninsula, with many pointing to the decadence and disunity of Dhenijansar as the principle reason that the Harimraj fell. Instead of old customs, many young officers and thinkers began calling for a new realm, a complete break with the old system of rajas, prabhi, and senapti, with only one centralized government. This concept, called Vanrahar or "Jungle Paradise", aimed to see our home remade stronger and purer than ever before, no longer divided arbitrarily but instead foremost among the nations of Haless. This proto-nationalistic theory would become the guiding philosophy of Tujgal's government in the late 16th and 17th centuries as the kingdom rebranded itself, to all the world, as Vanrahar.

Effects: Free Military Policies: +1.

Idea 7: Spice Plantation Colonization

In the deep rainforests of the ascension peninsula grow a multitude of plants with wondrous flavors and scents. While the carnivorous harimari never cultivated these spices in anything more than small decentralized parcels before, the Cannorian traders that began to arrive on the shores of Rahen in the early 1600s were willing to pay exorbitant prices for some of the rare seasonings that grew in the Ascension Peninsula.

By merging many of the smaller spice farms into sprawling centralized plantations with the Saffron Ordinance in 1623, the amount of valuable spices produced in southern Rahen nearly doubled over the following decade, leading to a huge influx of foreign trade.

Effects: Goods produced modifier: +10%.

Ambition: Tujgal Ambition

Effects: Land leader shock: +1.

Umdaj (R45) — Umdaj Ideas

Traditions: Umdaj Traditions

Effects: Land leader shock: +1; Cavalry recruitment cost: -15%.

Idea 1: Enduring and Strong

On the fringes of the great jungles of the Ascension Peninsula, Umdaj has endured hardships. The uprising of the slave state of Bhuvauri lost Umdaj their land, their trade routes, their coastline, and their honor. Our warriors were overwhelmed by the slaves, our overseers were complacent and unprepared. While it the uprising as a whole was a stain on the Raj, our people, our warriors believed that the death of their ruler at the hands of the slaves was a reflection on them. We are determined not to be caught off guard again.

Effects: Land morale recovery speed: +10%.

Idea 2: Following His Example

“Those who would seek to rule, must understand who they are ruling over and why they hold power. The Raja would have us all believe we serve because we were born to. Our kin deeper in the jungles believe it is because we are strong and others are weak. Yet, it is neither, it is because a ruler must do what is best for the country and its people, all of its people.

My great-grandfather was killed by the slaves because he treated them like chattel. Most would be overcome with a desire for revenge, to destroy those who had slain their sire, but not I. He was a fool, treat someone like they are naught but a tool to be used up and they will naturally turn on you to preserve themselves. Are we so different? We Harimari lash out at those who would intrude on our way of life, on our sacred lands, who would try to rule us. I will not make the same mistakes he did.” - Jadu of the Shining Tooth

Effects: National unrest: -2.

Idea 3: Living Land Tanks

While most mounts were unsuitable for Harimari, elephants proved both intelligent and sturdy enough for them to utilize. Over a long correspondence with the Ghavaanaji Reeshi, the skilled trainers and mages of Umdaj bred and raised increasingly larger and durable beasts -- calling them Rajathi, King of the Elephants. Some say they train not just elephants, but tie them to elephant spirits as well, perhaps in the way the Harimari themselves ascended. As one Harimari might equal a half dozen men in a fight, so do the Rajathi equal a half dozen of their normal sized kin.

Sadly, the Rajathi are so great in size that the land itself cannot support amounts in any great numbers and thus their use is limited to Umdaj’s elite warriors. These were armored on the front, and sported armor plated carriers housing a dozen or so Harimari warriors on either side of the beasts. When unleashed on the enemy’s lines, they would bulldoze all but the most dug-in defenders. This would then be exploited by the Harimari warriors, protected inside the carriers, who would leap out and savage the remaining stunned defenders.

As one Command General was heard to say after his troops had been on the receiving end of one of these charges, “Cats clearly don’t like being confined.”

Effects: Morale damage: +10%.

Idea 4: Open Minded for Harimari

Guru Suhan spoke of the merits of each philosophy and that none alone carried the answers we sought. We have seen this play out in our interactions with other races as well as other schools. While we Harimari might lord ourselves as the most suited to rule, there are many areas we lack. Our trainers were first taught by the northern states, their skills at raising elephants being peerless. Our ruler’s dealings with traders from nearby human Prabhi have brought a great deal of wealth and new ideas into our lands. Even to the point that the hard-liners amongst us struggle to argue against the benefits it has brought us.

While not all are equal in the Raj, we at least heed the words of Guru Suhan and see merit in utilizing the talents of those who prove themselves. The Prabhi’s young daughter has taken more than a few of his words to heart.

Effects: Female advisor chance: +33%; May recruit female generals: Allowed; Advisor cost: -15%.

Idea 5: A Winning Smile

There is a common belief that one should always carefully read Harimari contracts, especially the fine print. More than one naive merchant has found themselves inadvertently having sold not only their wares, but the building they were kept in thanks to a less than thorough read of the terms. However, the Shining Tooth clan who have ruled Umdaj for generations has garnered a reputation as relatively honest dealers… for Harimari. It is said that dealing with any Harimari with the shining grin of their fangs meant that one was going to get exactly what they bargained for.

Effects: Yearly corruption: -0.1.

Idea 6: A Gateway to the Raj

Located on the Dhenbasana’s great delta, Umdaj has been a gateway for trade and ideas flowing to and from the rest of the continent. River boats come and go laden with goods from the markets of Sarisung, all the way to the halls of debate. Sardipadhin silks, rare spices from the great delta, and new thoughts and ideas from Rayavhashapal all pass through our lands and every passage leaves a little of each on our doorstep. While we ourselves have spices and woodwork to offer, our place on the river has brought us far more than the jungles could. All the while, our shining smiles have brought with them acclaim for our honesty and fair play.

Effects: Global trade power: +10%.

Idea 7: An Unstoppable Force

During the battle of Seppadna, as part of the Varanhar coalition, Umdaj shock elephants smashed into the lines of the Command, Jaddari calvary then exploited the disruption and broke the lines of the reinforcements. Allowing for the coalition to break the siege of Khiraspid. Even amongst the legendary Jaddari calvary, the sight of a Rajathi charge, though rare, was a sight to behold. So large were the Rajathi that each plowed a stretch of the battlefield before it like a farmer’s plow tills a field. One Jaddari rider was heard to say, “Size isn’t everything.”

Effects: Cavalry shock: +25%.

Ambition: Umdaj Ambition

Effects: Years of separatism: -5.

Rabaghekhur (R50) — Rabaghekhur Ideas

Traditions: Rabaghekhur Traditions

Effects: Infantry combat ability: +10%; Prestige: +1.

Idea 1: The Black Tiger

'What the hammer? What the chain, In what furnace was thy brain? What the anvil? What dread grasp, Dare its deadly terrors clasp!

When the stars threw down their spears, and water'd heaven with their tears, Did he smile his work to see? Did he who made the Lamb make thee?

Tyger Tyger burning bright, In the forests of the night: What immortal hand or eye, Dare frame thy fearful symmetry?'

Effects: Shock damage: +10%.

Idea 2: Blood of Harimar

After the Disappearance of Harimar, the lands of the Ascension Peninsula were given to one of The Tiger King's grandsons, a proud and haughty warrior named Vijaysenar the Crouching Shadow. Though many lines of direct descent to the Progenitor have died out over the years, the lords of the Crouching Shadow dynasty still carry the blood of the progenitor over a thousand years later, and all of the glory and respect that comes with it.

Effects: Legitimacy: +1; Devotion: +1; Republican tradition: +0.3; Horde unity: +1.

Idea 3: Domains of the Oghaprabhi

An ancient system that is maintained in the Ascension Jungles to this day, each harimari lord is given a small amount of land to govern as exclusive hunting grounds upon reaching maturity and proving themselves to the Senapti.

This decentralized system has left the jungles largely undeveloped and deeply uncentralized, but it has had the benefit of making it far easier to exert some level of control over the dense jungles of the peninsula and to keep the many ambitious young harimari lords here occupied with squabbles against each other and not the throne.

Effects: High Caste Loyalty Equilibrium: +10%; National unrest: -1.

Idea 4: Long Waking from Torpor

For centuries the harimari of the Ascension Peninsula paid scarce attention to the outside world, instead focused on internal squabbles, tribal feuds, and personal aggrandizement. While the jungles made it difficult for any outside power to conquer them, the thousand petty fiefs of the Oghaprabhi were hardly a unified realm, and only a powerful hand could ever succeed in pointing all of the Peninsula’s efforts in one direction, and never for long.

This pattern of behavior finally began to change during the chaos of the mid 1400s, as the general unrest in the military and ineffectiveness of the central government shook the Senapti to action. Efforts by a new cadre of ministers under the young prince Adaraghir helped revitalize Rabaghekhur and turn its focus outwards from the jungles once again, and following the prince's ascension in 1464 Rabaghekhur began to rouse itself from its long period of inactivity and assert itself on the stage of Raheni politics.

Effects: Ruler administrative skill: +1.

Idea 5: Trade League of Sardika

In response to a surprisingly effective revolt in Sardika against the Bhuvaurite governor of the city-state in 1485, the newly energized Senapti came to the city's defense and expelled the occupying soldiers of Bhuvauri. The Senapti Adaraghir met with local city leaders, many of whom were fearful of reprisals from Sramaya, and agreed to establish a protectorate over the city if the councilors of Sardika would lend their wealth to strengthening Rabaghekhur. Whilst there were many rumors that the initial coup was instigated at the behest of Adaraghir, of course nothing could be proven conclusively...

Effects: Covert Action Cost Modifier: -20%.

Idea 6: Teakwood Hulls

Of the many great trees of the jungle, teak has proven to be one that is most useful for the nation. Notable for its hardiness and buoyancy, the trees are found commonly throughout the ascension peninsula, providing a wealth of resources that can be put to use building up the requisite navy for controlling the waves and the rich trade that sails upon them. As the Harimraj weakened, Rabaghekhur began to shift its gaze not north to Dhenijansar, but south - across the waves of the Gulf of Pearls, to the former Mengi-Raheni city states resting on the eastern coast of Sarhal.

Effects: Ship Durability: +5%.

Idea 7: Exile Kingdom of Meretgeban

While the chaotic years of the Wars of the Vizierate were a boon for Rabaghekhur’s ability act independently, it also allowed opportunistic outside powers to attack the isolated Senapti and Prabhi along the fringes of the Raj. In 1503, with the Raj in the final throes of the Vizerate Wars, Bhuvauri took their opportunity to pounce on an unprepared Rabaghekhur, burning its fleet in port at Sardika, and retaking the city once again.

This disaster was followed shortly thereafter by an opportunistic invasion of the mangroves of Pahruavan by the Prabhi of Tujgal, who had signed a secret agreement with the Bhuvauri government. These disasters collapsed support for the court of the ineffectual Senapti Bagherad, and soon the majority of the Oghaprabhi were declaring their allegiance to the White Tiger in Tujgal.

Fleeing from their ancestral lands, the former Senapti and his loyal retainers made their way across the waves of the Pearl Gulf to Sarhal, where they were well received by those cities who were former members of the Trade League of Sardika. Here, the exiled Bagherad would invest the wealth he had secreted away during his flight to attract loyalists, founding a small but effective mercenary company and plotting his return to his rightful place in Rahen. Though they would never retake their ancestral lands, in latter years his son Adaraghir II was invited to become King of Meretgeban, the Crouching Shadow becoming kings in a land far from home.

Effects: morale_damage_received：-10%.

Ambition: Rabaghekhur Ambition

Effects: Naval Force Limit Modifier: +20%.
